## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Anuvijjakassapaṭipatti* ("The Conduct of an Investigator" or "The short chapter on the resolution of conflicts") is the fourteenth chapter of the *Parivāra*, the closing analytical manual of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text outlines the necessary qualities, conduct, and proper character of a monastic inquirer or investigator who follows the Vinaya in resolving disciplinary issues and conflicts [SuttaCentral]. The chapter has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral notes a curated internal parallel with the *Upālipañcaka* (*Parivāra* 17), a relationship confirmed by automated text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus, which records 23 matching passages between the two texts, particularly between §1.1–1.5 and §28.2–28.3 [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus identifies 261 matching passages across 23 Pali works, demonstrating heavy reuse in Vinaya literature and commentaries, including extensive overlap with the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* (§1.1–4.2 matching §1017–1020), the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Vattakkhandhaka* (*Khandhaka* 18), and the *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares significant material with multiple numerical divisions of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*—predominantly the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10), *Aṭṭhakanipāta* (AN 8), *Ekādasakanipāta* (AN 11), and *Sattakanipāta* (AN 7)—as well as the *Visuddhimagga* and the *Padaṭṭhānahāravibhaṅga* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments generated by DharmaNexus also detect shared phrasing with the Sanskrit Sarvāstivāda *Dharmaskandha* as well as Tibetan Kanjur texts such as the *Ratnamegha-sūtra* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
